podcast.body: Mentioned by critic Greal Marcus as one of the impactful songs of the early 1970s, embodying the strength and clarity of black music during that era. "as clear and strong as Curtis may feel superfly in Freddy's dead."

podcast.body: This song, also a top 10 hit from the "Superfly" soundtrack, reached number four on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1972. It depicts the grim fate of Freddy, a junkie run over by a car, with lyrics like "Everybody's misused him, ripped him up and abused him, another junkie plan, pushing dope for the man." The song was nominated for a Grammy for Best R&B Song in 1973 but lost to "Papa Was a Rolling Stone." It could not win an Oscar because the version in the movie was instrumental and the Academy required songs to have words, leading to controversy over this rule. "Dead, hit number four on the Billboard Hot 172, it was an instrumental in the film."
